entries.title: Walking Pad Deals to Shop This Black Friday (2026)
entries.summary: Don’t let cold weather stop you from getting your steps in. These under-desk treadmills are on sale.
entries.content:
Black Friday is officially here, and plenty of great deals are live. Several walking pads are currently marked down, and with winter coming, now is the ideal time to take advantage of the discount. I, for one, have already started prepping my hibernation cave by stocking happy lights, arts and crafts, and a brand-new walking pad.

By the time December arrives, stepping outside might feel like taking a cold plunge. At that point, you’ll wish you had snagged a walking pad sooner to help you reach your step count goals without risking frostbite. Below, get a curated list of walking pad treadmills I have tested and vetted that are on sale.

Updated November 27, 2026: More walking pad and running treadmill deals were added. Prices and links were also updated.

The Best Urevo Walking Pads Are on Sale

The Urevo CyberPad is my favorite walking pad, and it’s on sale for $390 ($110 off). I’m confident in the product’s durability, mainly due to its sturdy-feeling build and comfortable belt. It offers a 14-percent incline, which is one of the highest available in walking pads, and the speed tops out at 4 mph. Unfortunately, the incline capability makes the machine difficult to store under furniture. It weighs about 71 pounds, so moving it around isn’t fun, but the wheels help. You can control the CyberPad with its remote control and companion app. You can also view your real-time metrics on the machine’s display.

The Urevo Strol 2S Pro is also on sale for $210 off. This 2-in-1 doubles as a treadmill with adjustable handrails, a display, and an attachable tablet holder. It was simple to set up, complete with a remote control and intuitive companion app. It feels super stable underfoot, even at top speed and incline level (7.6 mph and 9 percent). That top speed likely isn’t fast enough if you’re looking to sprint, but it’s plenty for a good workout. The machine is unobtrusive, has a quiet motor, and the 43-inch track is compact enough to place under your desk. Overall, it’s a sturdy walking pad treadmill that offers great value and range.

The Best Foldable Walking Pad Drops to $363

The WalkingPad C2 Foldable Walking Treadmill’s track is 32.5 inches when folded (and unfurls to 57 inches), making it a great option for storage in small spaces. It weighs 62 pounds, which isn’t light, but it makes for a sturdier running deck and a (hopefully) longer lifespan. You can adjust the speed via the remote control or companion app. Reviewer Kristin Canning found the app itself to be a little wonky. For example, if you don’t start a workout within the app, your data won’t sync. The app also saves each walking session separately, so if you take a break, you start from zero again. The good news is you don’t need to use the app to use the walking pad.

Canning also didn’t like that when you first start using the machine, you have to walk at slower speeds before you can unlock the upper end of the range. This might appeal to folks who enjoy gamifying their workouts, though. The app also offers workout programs that auto-adjust the speed to your pace via sensors under the belt.

More Walking Pad Deals

But you usually don't have to pay such a high price tag for a great model—you just have to wait for a good sale, and Black Friday deals have arrived, with the best sales you'll find before the holidays.

Black Friday is easily one of the best times to buy a robot vacuum, and Roborock makes one of the biggest ranges of robot vacuums that we love.   • If you want Roborock's arm attachment: Roborock Saros Z70 with OmniGrip for $950 ($700 off)

The Best Black Friday Vacuum Deals from Roborock

The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro launched in late summer as the newest addition to the brand's more affordable Qrevo line, and it quickly landed as a pick on my guide to the Best Robot Vacuums. It's often on sale for around $600, and thanks to Black Friday, it's down to the lowest price I've seen it for: $450, nearly half off.

Overall, Roborock's vacuums are great, but I've been especially impressed by this one's corner cleaning, thanks to its extendable mop arm. It won't always spot cords, but it does a better job at navigating furniture and getting underneath my cabinets than more expensive robot vacuums I've tested.

If you'd rather have a roller-mop-style robot vacuum, the Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow is another great option from Roborock's Qrevo line. This one came out in January of this year, and our reviewer instantly loved it.

The Qrevo Curv 2 Flow is a more expensive robot vacuum than the Qrevo 2 since it comes with the brand's SpriaFlow roller-mop. The internal roller spans nearly the entire width of the vacuum and can extend to edge-clean your home. It even has a built-in scraper to move dirty water into the tank instead of rolling it back onto the floor. If you're looking for an affordable mopping powerhouse, this is the one to choose. It's also nearly half off, down to $550 off the $1,000 price tag.

There's the affordable Qrevo line from Roborock, and then there's the higher-end Saros line. While neither I nor former WIRED reviewer Adrienne So were particularly impressed with the Saros 20, I've been much happier with the performance of the Saros 20 Flow. Like the Curv 2 Flow, it has a roller mop instead of spinning mop pads, and it did well in my mopping tests. It also didn't leave debris around, even with its high suction of 36,000 Pa.

It's one of Roborock's most expensive vacuums, and it comes across while using it—it feels very premium. I've been preferring it over the new Dyson robot vacuum I've been testing. Luckily, you can get it on sale right now for Black Friday. It still isn't cheap at $1,300, but it's one of my all-time favorites and one I have kept coming back to after trying other models.

If you're looking for something truly unique in a robot vacuum, Roborock's Saros Z70 might be what you're looking for. It has a mechanical arm built into it to pick up small items like socks while it vacuums, which sounds handy, but it didn't work as well as we'd hoped during testing. Still, maybe you feel that's the solution you've been dying for. If that's the case, it's available for a nice discount right now at $950.

It also packs 22,000 Pa of suction (not as powerful as the Saros 20 Flow, but still plenty of suction to clean carpets and rugs alike!) and still executes fast, effective cleaning. But the battery life on this vacuum isn't as long as that of other Roborocks we've tested. Again, you're mostly getting this one for the mechanical arm.

entries.content:
Merino Wool May be a super fiber well worth owning, but it isn't cheap. Right now, one of my favorite merino wool companies, Unbound Merino, is having its once-a-year sale. Unbound Merino's Black Friday sale is a great chance to round out your travel wardrobe with some excellent merino wool. Better hurry though, unlike most sales this time of year, Unbound Merino's Black Friday sale ends tonight.

From casual, everyday T-shirts, to underwear, socks, and great merino travel pants, Unbound has a little something for everyone. We've combed through the site and found a few of our favorite deals. Be sure to see our guide to the Best Merino Wool T-shirts, Best Merino Wool Clothes, and the Best Base Layers for more great merino wool options.

What’s So Great About Merino Wool?

Merino wool is great because you're stealing a sheep's ability to keep itself warm or cool based on the temperatures it's in. This is a process often referred to as thermoregulation. Merino sheep have thinner, softer wool than what most people think of when they think of wool. The sheep evolved this soft coat to keep them comfortable across a wide range of temperatures. The result is a fabric that's comfortable to wear next to your skin. For the softest tees, look for fabrics that are either superfine or ultrafine—anything 17 µm or higher—like Unbound's T-shirts.

Wool is sustainable, too. One sheep can produce 4 to 5 pounds of wool per year. While cotton has its place, and so does the occasional synthetic garment, merino wool is a remarkable fabric that's the cornerstone of my wardrobe. I don't think you can have too many merino pieces in your closet, but they’re not cheap, which is why we're featuring these deals.

What’s So Great About Unbound Merino?

I like Unbound's T-shirts because they're 100 percent merino wool, no synthetics involved. That means all the antibacterial, odor-resistant, moisture-wicking, temperature-regulating goodness of merino wool … just works. I've found Unbound's T-shirts in particular to be very quick-drying and wrinkle resistant, two of the reasons I think they're the best merino T-shirts for travel. The company's pants also have a very high wool percentage (95 percent), and they roll up nicely, making them very packable. Do you need special travel clothing? No, but Unbound's merino wool is naturally odor-resistant, which means you need fewer pieces in your bag. The company also offers a 30-day guarantee. If you don't like it, you can send it back.

How to Care for Merino Wool

Most merino products come with care instructions. Unbound Merino's T-shirts should be washed cold with like colors, then laid flat to dry. Whatever you do, don't bleach them and don't tumble dry them. The latter is especially destructive. I do it to every wool T-shirt I test, and it makes me sad, but I know some of you won't listen and will do it anyway, so I have to know what happens so I can warn you. Don't tumble dry. Just put it on a drying rack. It doesn't take more than a day. Seriously, you just spent $80 (on sale!) on a T-shirt; take care of it. Properly cared for, high-quality merino clothing like Unbound's is incredibly durable and will last for years. Throw it in the dryer and the pilling starts almost immediately.

Do I always lay them flat to dry? No. When traveling I usually hand-wash in the sink and then drape them over the shower curtain rod to dry, which hasn't seemed to have much negative impact. The issues with hanging wool to dry is that it will stretch out from the water weight. This is particularly true with 100 percent merino, like Unbound's T-shirts.

I've never had a problem storing merino in my closet between wears, but for long-term storage, I recommend you take precautions against moths, which are notorious for eating holes in wool. I have lost merino garments to moths. I make sure to wash and thoroughly dry whatever I am storing, then I seal it in a compression bag. Another option is to put your merino garment in a cotton bag or otherwise wrap it in cotton and then put it in a plastic bin. It's very important to make sure that the garment is completely dry before using any of these storage methods; otherwise your wool will smell musty and moldy. Other options include storing your garment in a cedar chest, which is a good natural deterrent for moths, or use moth traps or lavender sachets, which will repel the moths.

Unbound's T-shirts were my introduction to the brand, and they're still one of my favorite merino T-shirts. This T-shirt is incredibly soft, and because it's 100 percent merino wool, it'll stay odor-free for ages—as long as five or six days in my testing (depending on local temps, what you're doing, etc). Unbound's crew neck merino T-shirt has a relaxed, casual cut. It's not going for the technical look you'll get from many outdoor brands. It's also lightweight and packs down to a tiny ball, which is perfect if you're looking to simplify down to one bag. (Really, is there any other way to travel?)

The final thing I love about these is how fast they dry. In most climates, you can give it a wash in the sink at night, roll it up in a towel, wring it dry, lay it out flat, and it'll be dry by morning. If they have a downside, it's that Unbound's T-shirts do need to be babied a little. To help them last a long time I recommend hand washing and line-drying. Also note that while I like the merino crew neck, the V-neck is also on sale for $88 ($10 off).

Unbound's merino travel pants are a light and comfortable merino blend, with plenty of stretch and freedom of moment, thanks to the 5 percent elastane. These have a more formal look, what you might call slacks if you are a certain type of person. You might even be able to pull off going to office in them, but I'd sooner chew my leg off than work in an office, so I don't really know. I can say I've worn them to nice restaurants without a second look, and yet they don't scream “I've got money” when you're stumbling back to your hotel room in Prague at 4 am.

As you would expect from anything Unbound makes, these pack down fantastically small. You can pack two pairs of these for every pair of jeans. Again, for serious travelers looking to live out of a single carry-on bag, that's huge. The only downside is that these are on the thin side, not something you'd want to wear alone in cold climates. If you're like me and have to deal with winter, throw a good base layer underneath them and you'll be fine. The slim fit pant is also on sale if that's more your style.

Save More With a Bundle Deal

One of the best ways to save at the Unbound Merino Black Friday sale is to go for a bundle. I like this 1-Pack bundle, which gets you a T-shirt, underwear and socks for $125. There are quite a few other bundles as well, including the T-shirt 3-pack for $240 ($54 off) which is $20 cheaper than buying three T-shirts on sale, the boxer briefs pack for $75 ($15 off), and the sock 3-pack which is a steal at just $40 ($38 off).

Other Great Deals

Unbound's merino boxers are warm without being hot, great at wicking moisture, and capable of several wears without undue odors. 84 percent merino wool, 12 percent nylon, and 4 percent spandex, for a soft, stretchy, comfortable fit. They're 180 GSM (see our merino guide for exactly what GSM means), which makes them nice and light. The inseam here is 5.5 inches, and there's no tag, which is nice. The women's underwear is also on sale.

I prefer the short-sleeve T-shirts, but if you want a long sleeve, this is the T-shirt for you. It's essentially Unbound's short sleeve T-shirt, just long sleeve. All the same descriptions apply here, and many of the same multipack bundles are available. You can grab a 2-pack of long sleeve merino tees for $190 ($40 off).

entries.title: Best Dyson Vacuum Black Friday Deals for 2026: Up to $400 Off
entries.summary: If a Dyson vacuum is on yours (or a loved one’s) Christmas list, Black Friday is the best time to shop.
entries.content:
I’m often asked if Dyson products are really worth the money. As WIRED’s resident vacuum tester, I’ve tried every recent Dyson vacuum—from the newest, most powerful model to the long-favored V15 Detect—and I have a lot of thoughts on which ones you should buy and at what price. The best time to shop is during sale season, and lucky for you, Dyson Black Friday deals have arrived for you to scoop up a new stick vacuum or even a handy robot vacuum.

If a new vacuum is on your wishlist this holiday season, or a loved one's (my dad is obsessed with the Dyson), then Black Friday is your best shot at a great deal ahead of the holiday season. Here's the best sales happening on Dyson vacuums I've tested and love.

Want more deals? Check out our guide to the Best Black Friday Deals; our team is actively hunting all weekend long. Want more robot vacuum options? Check out the Best Roborock Black Friday Deals.

Updated November 27, 2027: This story has been updated for Black Friday with more deals, and we checked that prices are still accurate.

  • Best Dyson Stick Vac Deal: Dyson V16 Piston Animal for $800 ($180 off)
  • Another Great Dyson Stick Vacuum Deal: Dyson V15 Detect Absolute for $600 ($290 off)
  • Best Dyson Wet Floor Cleaner Deal: Dyson Clean+Wash Hygiene Wet Cleaner for $400 ($100 off)
  • Best Dyson Robot Vac Deal: Dyson Spot+Scrub Ai for $800 ($400 off)

The Best Black Friday Dyson Stick Vacuum Deals

If you’re going to buy a Dyson vacuum on sale, you might as well go for one of the better ones. The V16 Piston Animal is Dyson’s most powerful stick vacuum, with 315 air-watts of power, some nice quality-of-life improvements in the body design, and an option to add the Submarine 2.0 mop head. I really liked this vacuum for the design upgrades and power level, but the price tag can be hard to stomach. It’s on sale fairly regularly, and there are a few different on-sale combos: The base vacuum is $180 off, bundling it with the Submarine head is $200 off, and the option with the charging Floor Dok is also $200 off. I love the Submarine head, but while I haven’t tested the vacuum with the Floor Dok yet, it’s the accessory I want most—having your cordless vacuum fully charged whenever you want it, and somewhere to store it, is really handy.

If you want a cheaper vacuum that still comes with two cleaner heads, the older Dyson V15 Detect is also already on sale ($599), and it's even bundled with the Car Cleaning Kit, meaning three extra attachments. The V15 was our top Dyson vacuum pick for a long time because it's more affordable than the Gen5Detect and V16, but still packs two cleaner heads (the Digital Motorbar for carpet and Fluffy Optic for hard floors) and has 240 air-watts of suction (almost 100 more than the V10 Konical and other cheaper Dyson vacuums). It's a great all-around vacuum, and this bundle option gets you great extra attachments.

Dyson had two different budget vacuums come out this year, but the V10 Konical was my favorite of the two. It has a modified version of the All Floor Cones cleaner head you'll find on the much more expensive V16 Piston Animal and did a great job in my tests; overall, it actually scored a little higher than the V15 Detect when tested side by side. It's often on sale for $400, but you can find it for an even better $350 right now during Black Friday.

The PencilVac is incredibly handy and compact, and great if you're trying to do quick pickups daily on hard floors. You won't want it if you have any kind of rug or carpet, since it's only designed for hard flooring, but I did find it incredibly easy to grab and use for constant litter trails in my house. It's incredibly lightweight and a great fit for anyone with mobility or strength concerns. If these features speak to you, this is a great time to buy, as it's already on sale.

The Best Black Friday Dyson Wet Floor Cleaner Deal

This wet floor cleaner is often on sale for around $400, so it's not a huge surprise to see this deal ahead of Black Friday. The Dyson Clean+Wash is primarily a wet floor cleaner, but it can do dry cleans, too, and does not use a filter you inevitably need to keep clean. WIRED reviewer Kat Merck noticed no weird smells in three months of use. It's similar to the Dyson WashG1, with a self-propelled design that makes it easy to push around the room, and it does a good job scrubbing floors clean. Keep in mind that it's not great for dry debris, since it’s just rolling, not sucking.

The Best Black Friday Dyson Robot Vacuum Deal

The Dyson Spot+Scrub Ai came out earlier this year and is one of my favorite robot vacuums from the brand. That's including the newer Dyson R3 Nurovi Spot+Scrub UV I’m currently testing, which hasn't blown me away as a better investment. (It actually failed my corner test completely, which vacuums in that price range should not do.)

The Spot+Scrub Ai is much lower priced, and despite some dubious AI feature claims, it does a good job cleaning autonomously. It’s often discounted around this price, but the $400-off sale is a little better than what I saw during Prime Day.

entries.title: 16 Best Black Friday Headphone Deals (2026): Up to 57% Off
entries.summary: Get up to 57 percent off some of my favorite headphones and earbuds from Apple, Sony, Nothing, and more.
entries.content:
It is a great time to buy a new pair of headphones. Brands have largely finished launching their latest models for the year, and I'm seeing some stellar Black Friday headphone deals on new and older headphones alike. I've been reviewing headphones (and covering Black Friday deals) for more than four years, so I have a good handle on what's worth opening your wallet for. (Spoilers: it's Sony and Bose this year).

All the deals below are WIRED-tested products we stand by, including wireless earbuds and over-ear headphones. For more Black Friday deals, check out our guides to the Best Black Friday TV Deals and the Best Black Friday Mattress Deals.

Best Earbud Deals

Apple AirPods Pro 3 are the best wireless earbuds not only for anyone with an iPhone—but also for anyone who wants to keep things simple. They sound great and have some of the best active-noise-canceling (ANC) and transparency modes on the market. They also seamlessly sync with all of your Apple devices. At $100 off, it's the lowest price they've ever been at.

This is the lowest price I’ve ever seen on one of my favorite pairs of wireless earbuds. The Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro have one magic trick: call quality. To put it simply, I sound better talking on calls using these earbuds than any other I’ve tested, and it’s not a close competition. Beyond that, they’re solid all-rounders, with good noise-canceling, sound quality, and versatility.

Want workout earbuds that won't fall out? Get these Beats Powerbeats Pro 2. They're some of the more secure-fitting earbuds I've ever tested. Plus, they have great noise-canceling, transparency, and even built-in heart-rate sensors, so you can track your workout even if you left your fitness tracker at home.

The Nothing Ear (3a) are one of our favorite pairs of earbuds under $100, and 30 percent off is the biggest discount I've ever seen for them so far. They have a semi-transparent design and bold colors that stand out from the crowd (particularly the yellow version). While the automated noise-canceling isn't the best, it's hard to fault them at this new low price.

  • Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro for $170 ($80 off): Our go-to earbuds of choice for anyone with a Samsung Galaxy phone.
  • Shokz OpenFit 2+ for $100 ($100 off): Great open ear headphones at an exceptional discount.
  • Sony WF-1000XM6 for $248 ($82 off): If you want excellent sound quality in your ANC earbuds, these Sony earbuds have dynamic bass and clear, detailed treble.

Best Over-Ear Headphone Deals

My main gripe with the Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen) is price. At 45 percent off (their lowest price ever), that complaint vanishes, making this a top headphone deal to shop. The headphones are exceedingly comfortable and have excellent ANC—far better than basically every other set of headphones at this new low price of $200.

Did you hear the news? Sony made a version two of their cult-classic Sony WH-1000XM4 headphones. This is the first time they are on sale, and at $200, are one of the best deals this Black Friday. They have outstanding sound, great noise-canceling, a comfortable fit, and a convenient, folding design well-suited for travel.

The Nothing Headphone (1) are a home run in looks and sound, and they are at their lowest price ever ahead of Black Friday. They’re solid noise cancelers with a bold, transparent design on the ear cups that's somehow techy, retro, and futuristic-looking. Among their best features are the on-ear controls, namely the clicky wheel that adjusts volume and the flat rocker paddle that you can push back and forth to move to the previous track or skip ahead, respectively.

The budget Nothing Headphone (a) and premium Nothing Headphone (1) Pro are also on sale, but the Headphone (1) is the most appealing deal in my view.

AirPods Max 2 are excellent over-ear headphones for Apple fans, but the $550 sticker price is frankly absurd. Thankfully, they are almost always a little bit on sale, including now. This is far from the best deal I've seen on these headphones, and I do expect the price to dip further during Black Friday sales events, so I would add them to my cart and wait to pull the trigger.

My top over-ear headphone pick, the best-in-class Sony WH-1000XM6, is at its lowest price ever this Black Friday. These headphones are amazing across the board, with their high comfort, superior sound quality, and great noise-canceling capability.

  • Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) for $359 ($90 off): These are the best ANC headphones you can buy (read our review here), but the discount could be better.
  • CMF Headphone Pro for $49 ($30 off): CMF is Nothing's sub-brand, and this is a great deal on surprisingly capable, budget headphones.
